# routeur_routing_rule (Resource)

A routing rule in a workspace: when a gateway request matches, routeur.ai pins it to a model, auto-routes it with a quality bias, or fails over across several models. Rules are evaluated in ascending `priority`; the first enabled match wins, and the workspace's Default route (`routeur_default_route`) catches the rest. Every model a rule names must be activated in the workspace: take `provider` and `model` from `routeur_workspace_model`'s `provider_name` and `model_id` (rather than writing them out and adding `depends_on`), so Terraform activates the model before the rule needs it and keeps it until the rule is gone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "routeur_workspace" "support" {
  slug = "support"
  name = "Support"
}

resource "routeur_project" "helpdesk" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.support.id
  slug         = "helpdesk"
  name         = "Helpdesk"
}

# A rule can only name models activated in the workspace, and a provider's
# models need a credential first.
resource "routeur_provider_credential" "openai" {
  provider_name = "openai"
  label         = "prod"
  key           = var.openai_api_key
}

resource "routeur_workspace_model" "support" {
  for_each = toset(["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"])

  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.support.id
  model        = "${routeur_provider_credential.openai.provider_name}:${each.key}"
}

variable "openai_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Pin image requests from the helpdesk project to one model.
resource "routeur_routing_rule" "images" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.support.id
  project_id   = routeur_project.helpdesk.id
  name         = "Images to GPT-4o"
  priority     = 10

  match = {
    contains_image = true
  }

  action = {
    pin = {
      provider = routeur_workspace_model.support["gpt-4o"].provider_name
      model    = routeur_workspace_model.support["gpt-4o"].model_id
    }
  }
}

# Long prompts or prompts about invoices: two condition groups, either may match.
# Fail over between two models, retrying each once.
resource "routeur_routing_rule" "long_or_billing" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.support.id
  name         = "Long or billing prompts"
  priority     = 20

  match = {
    any_of = [
      { min_input_tokens = 20000 },
      { prompt_pattern = "(?i)\\b(invoice|refund)\\b" },
    ]
  }

  action = {
    failover = {
      strategy = "sequential"
      targets = [
        for m in ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"] : {
          provider = routeur_workspace_model.support[m].provider_name
          model    = routeur_workspace_model.support[m].model_id
        }
      ]
    }
  }

  on_failure = {
    retries      = 1
    wait_seconds = 1
    then         = "next"
  }
}

# Callers asking for "fast" get the cheapest model that clears a low quality bar.
resource "routeur_routing_rule" "fast" {
  workspace_id = routeur_workspace.support.id
  name         = "Fast alias"
  priority     = 30

  match = {
    requested_model = "fast"
  }

  action = {
    auto = { quality_bias = 10 }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `action` (Attributes) What the rule does with a matching request. Set exactly one of `pin`, `auto` or `failover`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action))
- `workspace_id` (String) Id of the workspace this belongs to (`ws_…`), e.g. `routeur_workspace.example.id`. The `routeur_workspace` data source resolves a slug to its id. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is evaluated. Defaults to `true`; removing the argument enables the rule again.
- `match` (Attributes) Which requests the rule applies to. Leave it out to match every request. Set conditions directly in `match` (all must hold), or list two to ten condition groups in `any_of` (at least one group must hold) — not both. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--match))
- `name` (String) Display name, unique in the workspace, 1–60 characters without leading or trailing whitespace. If left out, routeur.ai generates one from the rule when it is created; removing the argument later keeps the current name.
- `on_failure` (Attributes) Failure policy: retry the same target, then move on or return the error. Leave it out for the default behaviour. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--on_failure))
- `priority` (Number) Evaluation order, 1–999: lower runs first (the Default route owns 1000). If left out, the rule is placed after the workspace's existing rules when it is created; removing the argument later keeps the current priority. Priorities need not be unique: rules with the same priority run in the order they were created.
- `project_id` (String) Limit the rule to one project in the workspace (`proj_…`). Leave it out to apply the rule to every project in the workspace. A project must be enabled when it is newly targeted.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `id` (String) Public id of the routing rule (`route_…`).
- `slug` (String) Server-assigned and immutable; traces record a match as `rule:<slug>`.
- `updated_at` (String) When it was last changed (RFC 3339, UTC).

<a id="nestedatt--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action`

Optional:

- `auto` (Attributes) Let the auto-router pick the cheapest activated model that clears the quality bar. `auto = {}` uses the neutral bias. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--auto))
- `failover` (Attributes) Try several models, one after another or all at once. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--failover))
- `pin` (Attributes) Send matching requests to one model. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--pin))

<a id="nestedatt--action--auto"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.auto`

Optional:

- `quality_bias` (Number) 0 (cheapest) to 100 (smartest). Defaults to `50`, which is neutral.


<a id="nestedatt--action--failover"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.failover`

Required:

- `targets` (Attributes List) Two to five models, in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--failover--targets))

Optional:

- `strategy` (String) `sequential` (one at a time, in order) or `race` (all at once, first answer wins). Defaults to `sequential`.

<a id="nestedatt--action--failover--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.failover.targets`

Required:

- `model` (String) Model id at that provider, e.g. `gpt-4o`. It must be activated in the workspace: typically `routeur_workspace_model.<name>.model_id`.
- `provider` (String) Upstream provider slug: `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `deepseek` or `mistral` (new providers may be added). Typically `routeur_workspace_model.<name>.provider_name`.



<a id="nestedatt--action--pin"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.pin`

Required:

- `model` (String) Model id at that provider, e.g. `gpt-4o`. It must be activated in the workspace: typically `routeur_workspace_model.<name>.model_id`.
- `provider` (String) Upstream provider slug: `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `deepseek` or `mistral` (new providers may be added). Typically `routeur_workspace_model.<name>.provider_name`.



<a id="nestedatt--match"></a>
### Nested Schema for `match`

Optional:

- `any_of` (Attributes List) Two to ten condition groups, OR-ed; the conditions inside a group are AND-ed. For a single group, set its conditions directly in `match` instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--match--any_of))
- `contains_image` (Boolean) The request contains an image. Only `true` is a condition; leave it out otherwise.
- `min_input_tokens` (Number) The request has at least this many input tokens, 1–2,000,000.
- `prompt_contains` (String) The prompt contains this text, 1–200 characters.
- `prompt_pattern` (String) The prompt matches this RE2 regular expression, 1–500 characters. Stored verbatim.
- `requested_model` (String) The model the caller asked for equals this value, 1–80 characters.

<a id="nestedatt--match--any_of"></a>
### Nested Schema for `match.any_of`

Optional:

- `contains_image` (Boolean) The request contains an image. Only `true` is a condition; leave it out otherwise.
- `min_input_tokens` (Number) The request has at least this many input tokens, 1–2,000,000.
- `prompt_contains` (String) The prompt contains this text, 1–200 characters.
- `prompt_pattern` (String) The prompt matches this RE2 regular expression, 1–500 characters. Stored verbatim.
- `requested_model` (String) The model the caller asked for equals this value, 1–80 characters.



<a id="nestedatt--on_failure"></a>
### Nested Schema for `on_failure`

Required:

- `retries` (Number) How many more times to try the same target, 0–5.
- `then` (String) After the retries: `next` (the next failover target, or the next-best auto-routed model) or `error` (return the upstream error).
- `wait_seconds` (Number) Pause between retries: `0`, `1`, `5` or `30` seconds.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# id: <workspace_id>/<routing_rule_id>
import {
  to = routeur_routing_rule.images
  id = "ws_3/route_12"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <workspace_id>/<routing_rule_id>
terraform import routeur_routing_rule.images ws_3/route_12
```
